newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cash crudes edge up but buyers reluctant.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cash crudes edge up but buyers reluctant.

text.p: U.S. cash crude prices gained Friday, but market participants were relucant to buy as prices rose and ahead of the weekend, traders and brokers said.

Bellwether West Texas Intermediate/Cushing was up 20 cents at $19.35/45 late Friday, led by futures. Crude futures were driven up partly by a rally in gasoline, which many in the market said was related to trading positions rather than any shift in the weak underlying fundamentals.
"You only saw people doing business they had to do today. Most are taking a wait-and-see approach," said a Houston-based trader for a major oil company.

As well as the suspect rise on Friday, there is the prospect of market-moving development on Sunday if the United Nations and Iraq reach agreement to recommence exports under their "oil-for-food" deal.
U.N. and Iraqi officials are to meet on Friday in Baghdad to discuss the aid distribution plan, approval of which is necessary to restart oil sales.
"That's expected to go ahead but there could be a hitch, it could go either way and that's got people a little nervous," said a refinery crude trader.

Friday's business on domestic grades was at differentials little changed from late Thursday. West Texas Sour/Midland traded at $1.31 discount, Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James at a 20 and 21-cent premium and Eugene Island at a $1.46 discount.
Over the week, the sours were the big losers, with WTS and Eugene Island discounts depening by around 15 cents.

The shine was off LLS, which at moved up from around 19 cents last Friday to 25 cents premium mid-week, but headed lower as Norwegian state oil company Statoil arranged to send an Ultra Large Crude Carrier (ULCC) of North Sea Brent to the U.S. Gulf, as well as other deals struck to sell Cusiana and even bring Malaysian crudes in.
"You saw with the numbers earlier this week, there is still plenty of crude around and that's not going to get any easier," said a trader for a medium-sized integrated Texas firm.

American Petroleum Institute weekly data showed crude imports at just under nine million barrels a day last week and inventories nationwide rose by nearly 4.7 millin barrels. With crude runs heading down as product margins ease, traders see further pressure on crudes.
